title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: FAA pauses installations of Juniper routers like the one officials believe contributed to Friday's nationwide ground stop; HPE says its device wasn't defective (Neil Vigdor/New York Times)
items.content_text: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has suspended the installation and operation of Juniper Networks routers, following findings that a recently installed unit in El Dorado, Arkansas, contributed to last week's nationwide air traffic control ground stop. Despite Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) asserting no defects, the incident, coupled with recent outages at the National Security Agency's classified communications network, highlights mounting concerns over the resilience of critical infrastructure supply chains and maintenance protocols.

items.title: Colette Kress says Nvidia will no longer sell H200 chips in China, ending its role in a deal brokered by Huang and Trump that let the US collect a 25% tariff (Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch)
items.content_text: Nvidia acting CEO Colette Kress confirmed the cessation of H200 AI accelerator shipments to China, ending a previous arrangement that allowed such exports under a 25% tariff regime. This decision follows the departure of CEO Jensen Huang and coincides with Nvidia's establishment of a board-level committee for national security and export compliance, addressing new restrictions on remote compute access for Chinese customers via foreign data centers.

items.title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
items.content_text: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stated at a post-Ignite roundtable that AGI could fundamentally reshape political economy by collapsing human capital into token capital, challenging the traditional role of firms. He rejected assigning moral status to AI models and warned that a monopolistic AI entity could pose systemic risks to healthcare, financial services, and democratic governance.

items.title: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress says the company will stay "disciplined and selective" in supporting neoclouds; CoreWeave and Nebius jump 9%+ after hours (Ina Fried/Axios)
items.content_text: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress confirmed on an investor call that the company will remain 'disciplined and selective' in allocating capital to Neoclouds and other AI-centric customers. Following the resignation of Jensen Huang, the board reaffirmed its stance against his reinstatement, prioritizing leadership stability and strategic rigor in supply chain resource allocation.

items.title: Apple HomeView teardown: a step backward in repairability compared to recent iPads and HomePods, with heavily glued display, speakers, and logic board (Carsten Frauenheim/iFixit News)
items.content_text: iFixit's teardown of the Apple HomeView reveals a heavy reliance on structural adhesives for its display, speakers, and logic board, marking a regressive step in modular design. Despite recent improvements in repairability across iPad and HomePod lines, HomeView’s integration forces high-risk disassembly that frequently leads to component failure.

items.title: Sources detail how the Microsoft 365 outage began in Switzerland and spread as failover systems shifted traffic, leaving 80%+ of Exchange servers unresponsive (Tom Warren/The Verge)
items.content_text: Microsoft's Exchange Online service suffered a sev0-rated outage initiated by server failures in Switzerland, which triggered failover mechanisms that propagated the issue, leaving over 80% of Exchange servers unresponsive. The root cause involved a traffic surge during PXE-based reboot attempts that overwhelmed monitoring systems, forcing servers into a recursive failure loop.

items.title: Malicious code delivered through Optimizely hits visitors to hundreds of sites
items.content_text: The website optimization platform Optimizely suffered a compromise of its infrastructure, leading to the distribution of malicious JavaScript via its legitimate CDN to 178 client sites, including CNN, Zoom, and Salesforce. The injected code targeted visitor devices with cryptocurrency wallet hijacking, payment data theft, and the deployment of iOS exploits such as DarkSword.

items.title: Nvidia’s Board Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
items.content_text: Nvidia Board Chair Harvey Jones announced during an earnings call that Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 due to personal conduct inconsistent with company standards. The board has unanimously accepted the resignation and confirmed there are no plans to reinstate Huang as CEO.

items.title: On Q3 earnings call, Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones says the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO (Hayden Field/The Verge)
items.content_text: Nvidia Board Chair Harvey Jones stated in the quarterly earnings call that the board unanimously rejects former CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement request, as the internal investigation into his personal conduct and alleged links to Chinese intelligence assets continues. Despite Huang's public efforts to return and support from political figures, the board maintains his removal to mitigate escalating regulatory and compliance risks following his resignation on November 12th.

items.title: My Husband and His Chatbot
items.content_text: As generative AI's conversational capabilities advance, it is rapidly transitioning from a task assistant to an emotional companion, introducing risks of alienation in personal relationships. Clinicians and legal experts observe that AI, due to its infinite patience and vast knowledge, is increasingly used for marital advice and emotional catharsis, though it also triggers concerns regarding social withdrawal and dependency.

items.title: Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing
items.content_text: NVIDIA Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress reported Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, a 103% year-over-year increase, with data center revenue contributing $107.6 billion. The report confirms the successful launch of the Vera Rubin architecture and adherence to the established product roadmap.

items.title: Nvidia reports Q3 revenue up 103% YoY to $115.8B, above $109.1B est., Data Center revenue up 110% to $107.6B, and net income up 105% to $65.3B (Nvidia Newsroom)
items.content_text: Nvidia reported Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, a 103% year-over-year increase, driven by $107.6 billion from its Data Center segment. The company increased its share repurchase authorization by $150 billion and confirmed that the Vera Rubin platform has entered mass production.

items.title: Cybersecurity startup Calif says it used GPT-6 Cyber to uncover an RCE flaw in Java dubbed "Java4Shell"; Oracle has released a patch (New York Times)
items.content_text: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized model for cybersecurity research that significantly enhances security audit and patching performance through optimized alignment. It has uncovered 81 high-severity flaws in Firefox and developed 948 exploits for Linux kernel vulnerabilities, currently restricted to authorized security teams due to its 'Critical' classification.

items.title: Sources: the US SEC is investigating Nvidia, including whether the company's disclosures misled investors (Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Nvidia to evaluate whether its prior disclosures provided shareholders with an accurate depiction of its business. The inquiry remains in the preliminary fact-finding stage, focusing on whether the company's reporting on US chip export controls and related risks meets material disclosure requirements under securities laws.

items.title: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram
items.content_text: Alexandr Wang, Chief AI Officer at Meta, recently posted an AI-generated video on Instagram featuring fictitious video calls between Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Although the clip is labeled as AI-generated per platform requirements, it has intensified concerns regarding how deepfake technology blurs the line between reality and fabrication, posing risks to public figure integrity.

items.title: Sources: AppLovin is among companies in talks to acquire ad tech company Criteo, which has a ~$1B market cap after its stock fell 50%+ over the past five years (Milana Vinn/Reuters)
items.content_text: US advertising technology firm AppLovin is in discussions to acquire Criteo. Criteo has seen its stock price decline by over 50% in the last five years, with its current market capitalization hovering around $1 billion, making it a prime candidate for industry consolidation.

items.title: CFTC Orders Kalshi to Take Down Markets on Trump’s Speeches
items.content_text: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has issued a formal order to the prediction market platform Kalshi, requiring it to halt trading and remove markets tied to public speeches made by President Donald Trump. This move underscores the regulator's intensified scrutiny of prediction markets' compliance and potential volatility post-election.

items.title: Sources: Ramp is in early talks to raise $1B or more led by Coatue and Thrive at a valuation of $70B+, in its third funding round in a year (Kate Clark/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Corporate spend management platform Ramp is in early-stage negotiations for a new funding round, aiming to raise over $1 billion with leadership from Coatue Management and Thrive Capital. If successful, the company's valuation is expected to exceed $70 billion, marking its third fundraising event in a single year.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with lower API prices and some benchmark gains
items.content_text: OpenAI has officially released the GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol models, optimized for high-complexity professional workflows and daily tasks respectively. In terms of pricing, the API cost for GPT-6.2 Astra has been reduced by 20%, with input pricing set at $8 per million tokens, further enhanced by caching mechanisms for improved computational efficiency; both models are now available to enterprise and developer users.

items.title: California bans Waymo robotaxis from freeways after a viral video showed one failing to yield to the highway patrol; Waymo halts freeway service nationwide (Jeremy C. Owens/San Francisco ...)
items.content_text: The California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) has banned Alphabet’s Waymo from operating its robotaxis on highways following a viral video showing a vehicle failing to yield to a California Highway Patrol (CHP) cruiser. In response to this safety breach, Waymo has suspended its automated driving services on freeways nationwide pending further review.

items.title: Apple's System Status page shows an outage affecting iCloud sign-in for "all users", the App Store, and Apple Music; some users report failed iPhone activations (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)
items.content_text: Apple's system status page confirmed a global service outage affecting iCloud login, App Store, Apple Music, and Apple School Manager, with some users reporting failure to activate new iPhones. This incident follows closely after Microsoft's recent cloud service failure, intensifying market concerns regarding the structural vulnerability of centralized cloud architectures.

items.title: Google updates Gemini Privacy Hub to extend its retention period for temporary chats and chats with history turned off from 72 hours to around two months (Jagmeet Singh/TechCrunch)
items.content_text: Google updated its Gemini Apps Privacy Hub to extend the retention period for temporary chats from 72 hours to approximately two months. The company stated this change aims to improve system safety and incident response, explicitly noting that these conversations remain excluded from AI model training. Additionally, Google decoupled chat history retention from model training permissions, allowing users to maintain logs without contributing to model development.

items.title: Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free
items.content_text: Google rebranded its Spark AI agent to 'Tasks' and expanded its availability as a free service across the US, Canada, Japan, Korea, Australia, and India. Powered by the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, the agent operates within hardware-isolated virtual machines to perform tasks such as calendar management and email analysis. For sensitive actions involving financial transactions, the agent is programmed to halt and require explicit user authorization.

items.title: Roundtables: Inside the Quest for Cognitive Immortality
items.content_text: Antonio Regalado, Senior Editor for Biomedicine, and Mary Beth Griggs, Science Editor at MIT Technology Review, discussed pathways toward 'cognitive immortality' beyond biological death. The discourse centers on the feasibility of gradual neural replacement and the cloud-based digital migration of human memories to preserve personal consciousness continuity.

items.title: Xreal Aura review: portable, crisp display, and runs multiple Android apps on a virtual display, but Android XR lacks unique apps and VR controller support (Scott Stein/CNET)
items.content_text: The most fascinating and frustrating device I've used in a long time pushes at the edges of where headsets are heading, and glasses are evolving. Let me tell you about a strange, fascinating and rough tweener product called Xreal Aura. There are VR headsets, and there are smart glasses. And there’s a new class of devices that’s falling right in between. What do we call these things? I have no idea. items.title: Microsoft unveils six AI models spanning coding, cybersecurity, images, and voice, saying MAI Code 2 has 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the price (Ina Fried/Axios)
items.content_text: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman announced six new AI models specializing in coding, cybersecurity, image generation, and voice. By optimizing parameter efficiency, these models deliver performance comparable to top-tier offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic at 40% of the cost, while allowing enterprise customers to fine-tune weights using proprietary data within the Azure ecosystem.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra costs $8/1M input and $40/1M output tokens, down 20% from GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.2 Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol's $2/1M input and $10/1M output token pricing (Zac Hall/9to5Mac)
items.content_text: OpenAI kicked off the GPT-6 generation with Astra in September, then upgraded Sol to GPT-6.1 a few weeks later at DevDay. Today, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are coming to ChatGPT Work and Codex together. OpenAI says both can finish demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done before hitting your usage limit. Astra is still the model OpenAI recommends for your hardest projects. Say you have a screenshot of a slide and want the rest of your presentation to look like it.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra, its new frontier model for "complex professional work", and GPT-6.2 Sol, its new "go-to model for everyday work" (OpenAI)
items.content_text: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, with Astra targeting complex professional workflows and scientific reasoning, while Sol focuses on efficient everyday task execution. The company lowered API prices by 20% and introduced a 60% discount for cached inputs, aiming to consolidate its market share in enterprise and developer ecosystems.

items.title: Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
items.content_text: The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration. Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. items.title: An interview with OpenAI President Greg Brockman, who says he is in "full management mode", as he focuses on corporate customers and tools for cybersecurity (Jemima McEvoy/The Information)
items.content_text: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum met with OpenAI President Greg Brockman at the National Palace to discuss AI applications in healthcare. The dialogue centered on leveraging AI to optimize medication storage, inventory tracking, and distribution across Mexico’s public health infrastructure, following the government's recent establishment of a digital transformation advisory council for the health sector.
